messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High error rate and BGP route churn observed for azure-koreacentral -> private egress paths. Metric spikes: packet loss 6-12%, DNS lookup latency 500-800ms. PagerDuty incident INC-9876 created. Paging ops-oncall.

pagerduty: Paging: @emma (ops-oncall) - SEV2 - azure-koreacentral private egress degradation. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-9876

emma: I got the page, investigating now. Starting postmortem thread. Any customer-facing impact seen yet?

sanjay: Seeing spikes from our onprem-connected customers A, C and D. BGP neighbor resets 3x in past 12m.

lia: Noted. I can pull the VPN/ExpressRoute metrics and rtr logs. Starting with the vWAN control plane.

emma: Set severity to SEV2. Notify CS and on-call infra. @cust-success can you flag customers and open support cases?

cust-success: Opening tickets for customers A/C/D now. Notifying account teams. ETA for outreach 10m.

alex: From packet captures we see TCP slow-starts and RSTs to onprem appliances. Looks like intermittent path MTU/route churn.

emma: Useful. Lia — can you run a BGP summary on the egress routers? paste config/snippet.

lia: Running:
```
show ip bgp neighbors | include ki-neigh
Neighbor 10.12.34.5    AS 65001  established  00:12:34  flaps 4
Advertised routes: 1200  Received: 1189
Last error: Hold timer expired
```

lia: BGP hold timers are expiring, multiple flaps. Might be Azure fabric-level issue or vWAN controller instability.

emma: Good call. Tomas, can you check DNS behavior for our private zones that customers resolve over vpn? Use dig from koreacentral resolver.

tomas: Running checks:
```
> dig +short svc.customerA.private.redwood
10.45.12.3
; Query time: 622 msec
; SERVER: 10.1.2.3#53(10.1.2.3)
```

tomas: DNS queries are slow and occasionally time out from koreacentral. Upstream azure dns shows increased latencies.

support-bot: Auto-detection: correlated alerts from azure.monitor.network (vwan) and azure.dns. Created telemetry bundle at https://telemetry.redwood/internal/incident/1947654321

emma: Hypothesis: Azure network control plane instability causing route flap + DNS latency, affecting private egress for onprem circuits. Immediate mitigation options: 1) Failover affected customers to alternate vnet/region via secondary circuit. 2) Force BGP dampening at our edge to suppress churn. 3) Temporarily increase DNS TTLs / switch to our fallback resolvers for affected customers. Thoughts?

alex: Option 2 quick to test: apply conservative suppression on edge for prefixes from onprem peers for 15m, see if stability improves. If not, start failover.

emma: I'm going to notify Azure support now and request a vWAN controller health check + control plane event correlation. @sanjay coordinate with onprem contacts for scheduled failover if needed.

sanjay: Onprem ops confirmed they can flip to the secondary path, but it requires a maintenance window on their side (15m prep). Asking them to stand by.

pagerduty: Update: Azure support case AZ-23456 opened, assigned to Tier 2 network team. Expect 30-45m initial triage.

lia: Applying BGP dampening on our edge (temporary):
```
bgp dampening 200 3 15 60
router bgp 65100
 neighbor 10.12.34.5 route-map DAMP-IN in
```

lia: Applied. Monitoring.

emma: Good. Reduce alert noise and watch metrics. Also start capturing tcpdump on return path to validate.

alex: After dampening, observed drop in flap count from 4->0 for that neighbor within 3m. Packet loss trending down to 1-2%.

tomas: DNS still slow but fewer timeouts. Azure support reports they see 'control plane jitter' in koreacentral and are investigating a fabric update rollback.

cust-success: Customer A confirmed reduced error rates after our changes. They're still experiencing higher than normal latency but stable connections. Account team standing by to update.

emma: Since dampening helped, keep it for now but have rollback plan. Lia keep tracking. Also prepare runbook entries for failover in case azure returns degraded. Sanjay keep onprem ready.

sanjay: Onprem team can cutover in 20m if needed. They will test connectivity post-cutover and confirm.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: azure-koreacentral private egress - status INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATING (applied BGP dampening).

emma: Handoff note: I'm on call another 40m then handing to Lia for overnight watch. Lia — you own updates + postmortem draft. Key items to capture: timeline, Azure control plane events, impact customers, mitigation steps, temporary config changes, and RCA hypothesis.

lia: Acknowledged. I'll take ownership and create the interim incident report. Drafting timeline now and will attach telemetry links.

pagerduty: Reminder: SEV2 still open. If customer impact grows, escalate to SEV1.

tomas: Azure support just posted: 'we've rolled back a fabric change and are observing stabilization; monitoring for next 60m.'

emma: Great. Keep monitoring. Once stable for 45m and flaps = 0, we'll move to RECOVERY state. Lia — coordinate with cust-success to close customer tickets once verified.

lia: Will do. Preliminary mitigation successful. Leaving BGP dampening in place for 30m post-stable. Creating post-incident checklist.

cust-success: Customers notified of improvement. We'll keep watch and reopen if anything spikes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status MITIGATED -> MONITORING. Next automated check in 15m.

emma: Closing my shift — handing to Lia. Lia, ping me if anything regresses.

lia: Thanks! I'll update the incident page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-9876 and start the postmortem draft.

support-bot: Generated runbook diff for temporary config: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/diffs/1947654321. Remember to revert dampening once Azure confirms stability.

emma: Thanks team. Great work coordinating the fail-safe and customer comms. :thumbsup:
